visual_goal: Show that the platform's health, cost and exposure are decided where it meets registers, suppliers, portals and DMS products, with edge controls reporting back on the dealer's journey.
prompt: A left-to-right illustration. Far left: a generic dealer at a desk labeled 'Dealer journey'. One arrow right into a central block of small server tiles labeled 'Platform services'. Right of it, four external boxes stacked top to bottom: a building with columns labeled 'Registers', a crate with a plain euro coin marked '€' labeled 'Suppliers', a stack of web screens labeled 'Portals', and a server box labeled 'DMS'. One arrow from 'Platform services' to each of the four. Far right: a tall control panel with dials and switches labeled 'Edge controls'. Four arrows into 'Edge controls': from 'Registers' labeled 'confirmed outcome', from 'Suppliers' labeled 'cost per call path', from 'Portals' labeled 'confirmed state', from 'DMS' labeled 'reconciliation'. One long orange arrow along the bottom from 'Edge controls' back to 'Dealer journey', labeled 'journey SLO'. These seven labels plus the five arrow labels are the only words in the image.
alt: A dealer journey runs through platform services to registers, suppliers, portals and DMS; their confirmed outcomes, costs, states and reconciliation feed edge controls, which report a journey SLO back to the dealer.
